open_obligations.what_is_open: The first missing flagship invariant is preservation of \(\operatorname{Inv}(\kappa)\) under delayed context selection. Without it, neither full legal-order confluence, the first-failure colored-district theorem, nor strictly positive realization of every colored hedge can be derived.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen selection rule conditions a kernel and deletes activated labeled edges, but it neither augments the CADMG for selection-induced dependence nor supplies a closure theorem. Positivity only licenses normalization. Explicitly, let binary \(X,Y\) be independent and let a binary indicator \(R^\circ\) satisfy \(P(R^\circ=1\mid X=Y)=3/4\) and \(P(R^\circ=1\mid X\neq Y)=1/4\). Every joint cell is positive and the pre-selection kernel is Markov for the graph \(X\to R^\circ\leftarrow Y\), but \(P(X=0,Y=0\mid R^\circ=1)=3/8\neq1/4=P(X=0\mid R^\circ=1)P(Y=0\mid R^\circ=1)\). Thus conditioning on the indicator need not be Markov for the edge-deleted CADMG on \(X,Y\).
open_obligations.attempted: Ordinary adjacent-fixing commutation was applied only after adding the explicit Markov/provenance premise; strict positivity was used only for denominators. Label deletion and canonical replay do not repair selection-induced dependence, and aligning an arbitrary \(\mathsf W_j\) or \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\) witness with a graphwise failure would violate the directive.
open_obligations.partial_result: The conditional adjacent-swap lemma is proved, all operation words are retained, the Figure 3(b) SCM identity is proved without a trace claim, and \(\text{thm:pointwise-semialgebraic-completeness}\) preserves the exact coordinate and direct-score fiber-constancy theorem with strictly positive same-observed countermodel pairs.

prose_updates.tldr: For finite strictly positive regular-maximal labeled-missingness graphs, the durable result is an exact pointwise response-fiber decision: \(\operatorname{TCF}\) constructs finite semialgebraic partitions for every interventional coordinate and for the declared score contrast, returning a unique value graph exactly when the target is constant on the compatible fiber and otherwise certifying a positive same-observed countermodel pair. The response variables preserve each individual bidirected-edge factor and every label deletion. Raw colored traces are only expression proposals, and a rational expression is published only after a whole-cell equality check; graphwise colored-recursion completeness and colored-hedge realization remain open because delayed selection has not been proved to preserve the CADMG Markov/provenance invariant. The Figure 3(b) observed-law identity, the de Aguas Proposition 4 strict extension on the finite EIPFD family, and the Mokhtarian root-control embedding are retained. Relative to Duarte et al., the response-CAD layer is an lm-specific constrained specialization, not a claimed strict extension.

project_justification.gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and motivate the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select identity; Mokhtarian et al. give completeness for observed root controls; Duarte et al. give a general finite response-function polynomial-programming framework. What is not yet available is a proof that delayed selection preserves a trace-aware nested-Markov kernel and that every graphwise colored failure yields a strictly positive colored-hedge pair.
project_justification.niche: On finite full-positive lm-SCM fibers, individual-edge-factorized response polynomials and exact real-closed-field elimination give a complete pointwise constancy test while respecting label-specific table equalities. This is a constrained lm specialization of response-function programming, with raw trace expressions serving only as verified annotations.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the two-way lm-SCM/response-polynomial fiber equivalence, separate coordinate and direct-score semialgebraic partitions, exact positive countermodel pairs, an explicit finite termination bound, whole-cell soundness, the Figure 3(b) SCM identity, and theorem-level comparator reductions. It explicitly withholds branch confluence, graphwise colored-hedge completeness, and hedge realization.

sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of every finite full-data cell makes the displayed observed conditionals, selected-cell normalizations, and response-fiber inequalities well defined. Positivity does not imply that a conditioned kernel is Markov for the edge-deleted CADMG.

prose_updates.related_work: De Aguas et al. (2025), Proposition 4 and Figure 3(b), are the first lm-specific comparator: the proposition gives a sufficient weighted context formula, while Figure 3(b) motivates the independently proved identity \(Q_a(y)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=y\mid A=a,R_W=0)\). Mokhtarian et al. (2022), Theorem 1 and Corollary 2, give soundness and completeness when context variables are observed causal roots; the present theorem embeds that functional on the common finite positive domain but makes no strictness claim over its full domain. Duarte et al. (2023), Proposition 2 and Theorem 1, place finite causal queries in response-function polynomial programming, including bounds and point-identification cases. The response-CAD layer here is a constrained specialization that adds label-compatible one-hot tables and independent simplices for each individual bidirected-edge and private factor; no non-subsumption claim is made. Richardson et al. (2023), Lemma 30, gives ordinary adjacent-fixing commutation for a Markov kernel. The conditional colored lemma transports specialized provenance only under an explicit invariant and does not merge trace words. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) establish ordinary hedge completeness, but the adaptation to endogenous missingness colors, delayed selection, and strict positive individual-edge realization remains open. Tikka et al. and Bhattacharya et al. inform sound search and missing-data recursion but do not close that adaptation.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The first unresolved step is delayed-selection preservation of the trace Markov/provenance invariant. Conditioning on a missingness indicator can induce dependence between its parents, while the frozen update merely deletes activated labeled edges and does not augment the CADMG. Consequently, full legal-order confluence, the first-failure colored-district theorem, and universal strictly positive colored-hedge realization are not proved. The algebraic witness compiler remains a finite diagnostic and is never aligned with a graphwise failure. The pointwise CAD theorem is independent of this gap because every annotation is universally verified on its fixed semialgebraic cell. Continuous alphabets, nonpositive support, ordinary computation on unencoded reals, and polynomial-time complexity remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The graph, labels, finite alphabets, treatment, outcome, and score map are supplied. The proved identification result is pointwise semialgebraic completeness on the finite, strictly positive, regular-maximal, individual-edge semi-Markovian subclass: a coordinate or score contrast is returned exactly when it is constant on the observed-law fiber, and a negative cell has two strictly positive same-observed models with different target values. Exact interfaces are needed only to select a represented cell or extract a represented pair. The Figure 3(b) proposition proves the SCM functional identity but not a complete legal colored operation word. Raw trace states are not assumed certified, distinct words are not merged, and the compiler returns no colored hedge. The de Aguas criterion is strictly extended on the finite EIPFD family, root-control is embedded on the common domain, and Duarte response programming is the broader paradigm within which the response-CAD layer is constrained. No graph-learning, estimation, finite-sample inference, continuous-state, graphwise colored-completeness, or polynomial-time result is claimed.
